items.stem: A company says 'we only use a third-party AI tool, so the EU AI Act does not apply to us.' Why is that risky?

options.text: Obligations can attach to deployers, not only providers, so using an AI system can still create duties
options.rationale: Correct: the Act allocates obligations by role, and deployers of high-risk systems have duties too.

options.text: The Act applies only to companies headquartered in the EU
options.rationale: Its reach can extend to systems used or placed on the EU market regardless of HQ.
Risk depends on use, not on whether the tool was bought.
Coverage is not limited to open-source systems.

items.explanation: Correct: the Act allocates obligations by role, and deployers of high-risk systems have duties too.

items.stem: Which TWO are commonly cited obligations associated with high-risk AI systems? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Maintaining technical documentation and records about the system
options.rationale: Correct: documentation and record-keeping are high-risk obligations.

options.text: Ensuring appropriate human oversight of the system
options.rationale: Correct: human oversight is a high-risk obligation.

options.text: Publishing the full model weights openly
options.rationale: Open weight publication is not a high-risk obligation.

options.text: Guaranteeing zero errors in all outputs

items.explanation: Correct: documentation and record-keeping are high-risk obligations.

items.stem: The same large language model powers a spam filter and a tool that screens job applicants. How should risk tier be assigned?

options.text: Per use: the applicant-screening use is likely higher-risk, while the spam filter is likely lower-risk
options.rationale: Correct: the Act's risk tier depends on the use context, not the underlying model alone.

options.text: Both are high-risk because they share a model
options.rationale: Risk is assessed by use, not by shared components.

options.text: Both are minimal-risk because it is one model
options.rationale: A shared model does not make every use minimal-risk.

options.text: Risk cannot be assigned until regulators rule
options.rationale: Organisations are expected to classify uses themselves.

items.explanation: Correct: the Act's risk tier depends on the use context, not the underlying model alone.
